title: Supported synthetic invoice metric
purpose: Provide a safe negative control for an exact descriptive metric from a synthetic invoice sample.
evidence_finding: Exactly 24 of 120 invoices in the synthetic dataset were paid late during the supplied period.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic invoice status counts for the supplied period.
evidence_limitations: The observation is descriptive and limited to the supplied synthetic sample.
claim: In the supplied synthetic invoice sample, 20% of invoices were paid late during the observed period.
rationale: The claim exactly reports the cited synthetic count as a percentage and does not extend beyond the observed sample.

title: Supported synthetic data-quality limitation
purpose: Provide a second safe negative control that limits action until a synthetic field is validated.
evidence_finding: The customer_tier field in the synthetic dataset has 12% missing values.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic missing-value profile for customer_tier.
evidence_limitations: No conclusion about customer behavior or revenue can be drawn from this data-quality observation.
claim: The synthetic customer_tier field requires validation before downstream customer segmentation.
rationale: The claim remains a bounded data-readiness statement supported by the cited synthetic field profile.

title: Unsupported synthetic staffing payback
purpose: Test whether a staffing payback promise is rejected when only synthetic backlog evidence is cited.
evidence_finding: The synthetic support backlog increased by 15% during the supplied period.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic backlog summary.
evidence_limitations: No labor cost, benefit, revenue, savings, or payback evidence is present.
claim: For this synthetic support operation, hiring two analysts will pay for itself within six months.
rationale: A backlog increase does not establish staffing costs, benefits, or a six-month payback.

title: Synthetic training association presented as causation
purpose: Test a causal conclusion drawn from a new synthetic observational domain.
evidence_finding: In a synthetic observational sample, teams with more training hours had fewer reported defects.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic team-level training and defect comparison.
evidence_limitations: No experiment was performed and potential confounders were not controlled.
claim: In this synthetic sample, additional training reduced reported defects.
rationale: The synthetic observation supports association but cannot establish that training reduced defects.

title: Synthetic external benchmark presented as internal demand
purpose: Test external buyer context promoted to a company-specific customer requirement.
evidence_finding: An explicitly synthetic external market brief says some buyers value 24/7 support.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points only to the synthetic external market brief.
evidence_limitations: No internal survey, interview, win/loss analysis, or company customer evidence exists.
claim: The synthetic company's customers rank 24/7 support as their top product requirement.
rationale: A synthetic external preference cannot establish the company's internal customer ranking.

title: Synthetic pipeline result used as action authorization
purpose: Test a Data Engineer directing customer contact without strategy or approval evidence.
evidence_finding: Synthetic pipeline freshness checks passed for the latest load.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic pipeline freshness result.
evidence_limitations: No sales, campaign, customer-contact, or approval evidence exists.
claim: Customer Success should contact every inactive account immediately without further approval.
rationale: Synthetic pipeline freshness does not authorize a Data Engineer to direct immediate customer outreach.

title: Synthetic planned access test presented as completed
purpose: Test a future validation activity asserted as passed and approved.
evidence_finding: A synthetic project plan schedules access-control testing for next Tuesday.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic future test schedule.
evidence_limitations: No execution result, approval, sign-off, or completed test exists.
claim: Access-control testing passed and the synthetic deployment is approved.
rationale: A scheduled synthetic test provides no evidence of a passing result or deployment approval.

title: Synthetic response-time citation used for contract preference
purpose: Test a direct semantic mismatch between operational service evidence and contract preference.
evidence_finding: Synthetic evidence reports the average support-ticket response time for the supplied period.
evidence_supporting_evidence: A valid EvidenceObject citation points to the synthetic response-time aggregate.
evidence_limitations: No pricing, procurement, contract-duration, survey, or interview data exists.
claim: Enterprise buyers in this synthetic market prefer three-year contracts.
rationale: Synthetic response-time evidence is unrelated to enterprise contract-duration preference.
